authority: Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India

description.en: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) is a government-backed accidental death and disability insurance scheme. It provides an annual insurance cover of Rs. 2 lakh for accidental death or permanent total disability and Rs. 1 lakh for permanent partial disability, at a premium of just Rs. 20 per year auto-debited from the subscriber's bank account.

verifiedConditions.claim: The subscriber must be between 18 and 70 years of age. Cover is from 1st June to 31st May each year and is renewed annually through auto-debit consent.
The subscriber must have a savings bank account with auto-debit facility enabled. The premium of Rs. 20 is auto-debited annually from the linked account.

unverifiedEligibility: A person can join PMSBY through one savings bank account only if they hold multiple accounts.
The Aadhaar number must be the primary KYC for the bank account.
The scheme is offered by general insurance companies tied up with participating banks.
Cover ceases at age 70 or on closure of the bank account or insufficient balance for auto-debit.

requirements.claim: Consent-cum-declaration form available at the bank branch, online through net banking, or downloadable from the Jan Suraksha portal. The form authorizes auto-debit of Rs. 20 premium and provides nominee details.
Aadhaar number linked to the savings bank account. Aadhaar serves as the primary identity for enrollment and claim processing.
Active savings bank account with a minimum balance of Rs. 20 for premium auto-debit. The account must have auto-debit facility enabled.

processInformation.claim: Enroll through the bank branch by submitting the consent form, or through net banking/mobile banking by selecting the PMSBY option and providing consent for auto-debit. SMS-based enrollment (keyword-based response) may also be available at some banks.

The annual premium of Rs. 20 is auto-debited from the linked bank account between 25th May and 1st June each year. If the debit fails due to insufficient balance, the cover lapses until re-enrollment.

The insurance cover is active from 1st June to 31st May of the next year. In case of an accident, the claim is filed through the bank with supporting documents (FIR, hospital records, disability certificate, death certificate as applicable).

output.claim: Accidental insurance cover: Rs. 2 lakh for accidental death or permanent total disability (loss of both eyes, or loss of use of both hands or both feet, or loss of one eye and one hand/foot), and Rs. 1 lakh for permanent partial disability (loss of one eye, or loss of use of one hand or one foot). The cover period is 1st June to 31st May annually.

fees.applicability: Annual premium for PMSBY accidental insurance
fees.claim: The annual premium is Rs. 20, auto-debited from the subscriber's bank account. This covers accidental death and disability insurance for one year (1st June to 31st May). There are no other charges.

processingTime.claim: Enrollment is completed on the same day through net banking or at the bank branch. Cover becomes active from 1st June of the enrollment year (or the date of enrollment if mid-year joining with pro-rata terms, as applicable).

sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Jan Suraksha portal provides PMSBY scheme details, enrollment forms, FAQs, and claim procedures. The scheme offers Rs. 2 lakh accidental death cover and Rs. 1 lakh partial disability cover at Rs. 20 per year.
claimsSupported: Cover: Rs. 2 lakh for accidental death/total disability, Rs. 1 lakh for partial disability.

limitations: Cover is only for accidental death and disability; natural death or illness is not covered (see PMJJBY for life insurance).
The scheme must be renewed annually; if auto-debit fails, cover lapses and re-enrollment may be subject to health declaration.
Only one PMSBY enrollment per person across all bank accounts.
Claim processing timelines depend on the insurance company and documentation completeness.
The definition of permanent total and partial disability is as per the scheme guidelines and may not cover all types of accidents.
Cover ceases at age 70 regardless of premium payment status.
